messages:
Anya K: Quick heads-up from profiling: after the kernel-switch we rolled yesterday, prefix cache behavior regressed. P95 cold-prefix latency climbed from ~420ms -> ~1150ms and kv hit-rate on our synthetic prefix set fell 38% -> 21%.
Luis: Yikes. Any signal whether this is batching/kernels or keying?
Anya K: Both. Kernel selection changed the short-seq fast path so requests are getting routed to a slower kernel on miss. Also discovered fragmentation in prefix keys: subtle tokenizer normalization change means a lot of near-duplicate prefixes are hashing differently.
MJ: Can you paste the minimal repro?
Anya K: repro script below (runs synthetic requests hitting top prefixes):
```bash
python tools/synth_hitrate.py --model rwd-small --seed 42 --prefix-corpus examples/prefixes.txt --concurrency 20 --requests 10000
```
Logs show batch mean size +1.4x after switch and kv lookup latency per-request increased for the first position in the batch (kv.pos=0).
Samir: If kernel choice is the trigger, we should test a quick mitigation: 1) canonicalize keys before hashing 2) force the short-seq kernel on miss for a canary rollout. Also consider how autoscale ramps interact.
deploy-bot: scheduled job "kv-priming" queued by Samir at 2026-03-18T15:24:00Z (job id kv-priming-3555).
Elaine: What's the proposed experiment matrix?
Luis: My suggestion: run a 24h A/B on dev cluster with three arms: 
  A) current kernel-switch + no-key-normalizer (control)
  B) key-normalizer only (trim, unicode NFKC, collapse spaces)
  C) key-normalizer + short-seq kernel override on miss
Measure: kv.hitrate, kv.latency_by_pos, batch.size.hist, cold P50/P95 token latency, and token-cost.
MJ: Also add instrumentation that breaks out KV lookup latency by batch position (first/last) and by seq-length. I suspect async IO scheduling + larger batches pushes the lookup behind other work.
Anya K: I added the dashboard panels: kv.hitrate, kv.pos_latency, batch.size.hist. Attaching diff in the PR for the key-normalizer (small patch to pre-hash step).
Samir: For warmup strategy experiments, let's avoid one-shot full prepop. Instead try a staged approach during deploy and autoscale: 
  - On node-add events, seed top-200 hot prefixes to the new node immediately (cheap probe)
  - Then run a sampled distributed fill over 10 minutes hitting top-2k prefixes
  - Run low-qps scheduled micro-primers every 5m during the first hour of rollout for redundancy
This reduces immediate fill cost and keeps hit-rate improving as capacity stabilizes.
Elaine: Cost / safety caveats?
MJ: Quick estimate: micro-primers ~120 USD/day per cluster if we run the low-qps jobs every 5m. Need budget PR if we adopt cluster-wide. Also ensure primers respect rate limits and don't affect real traffic.
Luis: Important: the key-normalizer must be hash-stable and cheap. Implement canonicalization that preserves placeholder tokens and only touches whitespace/unicode. Avoid canonicalizations that create new tokenization edge-cases.
Samir: I'll own the prepopulate job and can run a canary on 2 nodes first. Plan: run staged fill on canary, monitor kv.hitrate and P95, then expand.
Anya K: I'll open the PR with tests, the normalizer, and the deploy hook for staged prepopulate. Also adding metrics: kv.hitrate_topk, kv.latency_by_pos, prepop.cost_est.
deploy-bot: rollout window scheduled: 2026-03-19T02:00Z -> 2026-03-19T04:00Z.
Elaine: Sounds good — ping me when PR is up so I can review the deployment constraints.
Luis: Small follow-up: add a canonical hashing test vector set so we don't regress again on tokenizer changes.
Anya K: Will add tests and a small synthetic golden corpus. Will post canary results here after the run.
Samir: Thanks — I'll coordinate the scheduled job and the canary nodes.
MJ: Thanks team. Short-term: prioritize key-normalizer + staged prepopulate for the canary.
